discrepancies.explanation: Two desktop-host tests failed. One (v41, concurrent starts) passes when its file runs alone: it depends on machine load, as 5.6 reported for two other host tests. The other (v47, dashboard live monitor) fails alone too, with the unmodified 5.6 programs, on this machine.

discrepancies.item: v47 dashboard live monitor (a defect of 5.6, not of the test)
discrepancies.found: The desktop host reports the elapsed training time of /api/mw/status with three decimals. A training segment shorter than half a millisecond is reported as 0, the dashboard then has no throughput for it (null), and the test requires a positive throughput. 5.6 made training fast enough for the first 100 updates of the three-player river game to take less than that on this machine.
discrepancies.repairIn57: server.c reports the elapsed time with six decimals (microseconds). The 5.7 host passes the test.

discrepancies.item: Windows thread check of validate_windows56.ps1 (found by reading the script)
discrepancies.found: Section 4 trained golden spec g05-flop6 (8 deals per update) with 1 to N threads. 5.6 used several threads for an update only when state visits per deal times deals per update reached 2,000, which this spec never does after its first update, so the check compared single-threaded runs with each other.
discrepancies.repairIn57: validate_windows57.ps1 uses a 64-deal spec with hand groups and forces every update onto all threads (EIGHTMAX_THREAD_CHOICE=fixed); the engine reports the threads used.

discrepancies.item: Thread-count dependence under a very small table budget (5.6 behaviour, documented in 5.7)
discrepancies.found: The workers' transient memory comes out of the table budget. With a budget of 1 to 2 MiB the update at which training stops depends on the number of worker threads (for example flop3-kings with 64 deals per update and 2 MiB: 12 updates with 1 to 4 threads, 0 with 8). States are identical for every thread count as long as the budget is not reached.
discrepancies.repairIn57: none (behaviour preserved); 5.7 reproduces 5.6 at every thread count, and the 5.7 tests compare stopped trainings at equal thread counts.

wine.notes:
The Windows executables of the final build under Wine 9.0 (validation/5.7/wine57.sh), Linux container. Wine is not Windows: class 2.
- selftest57-wine.json   mwcli.exe --selftest57: the step "Run 5.7 Windows validation.bat" runs first.
- v57.test.tap           the 5.7 regression file with mwcli.exe and EightMax.exe in place of the Linux programs. Three of its tests compare with the archived 5.6 LINUX binary, which runs natively: they compare the Windows build of 5.7 with the Linux build of 5.6 (frozen-batch states for 1 to 8 threads, sampled and exact evaluations, complete studies).
- v56.test.tap           the 5.6 regression file, the same way.
The whole suite was not run under Wine for 5.7. 5.6 ran it: 514 passed, 68 failed, 1 skipped, every failure also present with the 5.5 Windows programs under the same harness (VALIDATION-5.6.md).

stabilitySixMinutes.explanation: the tool's long study has a budget of 20,000,000 deals per seed; with 322 s left a seed reached the engine's limit of 10 million updates per training and the study ended with an error instead of at its time limit. The unchanged 5.6 binary fails in the same way with the same command (validation/5.7/stability/README.md).

knownDefectsFound.what: A study whose budget exceeds 10,000,000 deals per seed (one deal per update) fails with "Iteration count must fit the 10 million iteration limit" when a seed reaches the limit, instead of being refused when it starts.
knownDefectsFound.workaround: keep study budgets at or below 10,000,000 deals per seed (the shipped fixtures stop at 4,000,000); with frozen batches the limit is 10 million updates, that is 640 million deals at 64 deals per update
